lessons.title: Getting ready to sow
lessons.html:
Before you sow

Many ornamental plants, like marigolds, petunias, alyssum, Namaqualand daisies and many indigenous plants, are grown from seed in a nursery. Good preparation gives strong seedlings.

Check your instructions

Your supervisor will tell you which seed to sow, how many trays to fill and where to put them. Read the seed packet. It tells you the plant name, how deep to sow, and how long the seed takes to come up.

Gather your tools and materials

  • Clean seed trays or punnets
  • Seedling mix (fine, clean growing medium)
  • The seed, in its labelled packet
  • A flat board or presser to level the mix
  • Labels and a pencil or waterproof marker
  • A watering can with a fine rose, or a fine mist nozzle
  • Fine vermiculite or sifted mix to cover seed

Clean trays

Dirty trays carry fungus that kills seedlings. This disease is called damping off. Wash old trays, scrub off old soil and let them dry. Use the cleaning product your supervisor gives you and follow the label.

Fill the trays

  1. Loosen the seedling mix so there are no lumps.
  2. If the mix is very dry, wet it a little first so it is damp, not muddy.
  3. Fill the tray to the top.
  4. Tap the tray on the bench to settle the mix.
  5. Scrape off extra mix with a flat stick.
  6. Press lightly with the board so the surface is flat and firm, about 1 cm below the rim.

Work safely

  • Wear gloves when handling growing mix. It can carry germs.
  • Wear a dust mask when mixing dry medium, so you do not breathe in dust.
  • Some seed is coated with chemicals. Do not eat or drink while working with seed and wash your hands afterwards.
  • Lift heavy bags of mix with a straight back and bent knees, or ask for help.

lessons.title: Sowing seed by hand
lessons.html:
Sowing the seed

Sowing means putting the seed on or into the growing mix. The aim is to spread seed evenly so seedlings do not grow on top of each other.

Label first

Write a label before you sow. Put the plant name, the date and your name or team on it. Push it into the tray at one end. A tray with no label is a problem later, because many seedlings look the same.

Sowing different seed sizes

Seed sizeHow to sow
Fine, dust-like (petunia, lobelia)Mix with a little dry sand and sprinkle on top. Do not cover, or cover very lightly.
Medium (marigold, zinnia)Sprinkle evenly or place in rows. Cover with a thin layer of fine mix.
Large (sweet pea, nasturtium)Push each seed into the mix one by one, about two times as deep as the seed is big.

Steps

  1. Pour some seed into the palm of your hand or onto folded paper.
  2. Tap gently with your finger so the seeds fall one by one.
  3. Move across the tray evenly. Do not drop many seeds in one spot.
  4. For plug trays, put one or two seeds in each cell.
  5. Cover the seed to the depth on the packet, using fine vermiculite or sifted mix.
  6. Press lightly so the seed touches the damp mix.

Do not waste seed

Some ornamental seed is very expensive. A small packet of F1 hybrid seed can cost hundreds of rand. Close the packet after use and return it to the seed store. Never leave open seed in the sun or where it can get wet.

Common mistakes

  • Sowing too thickly, so seedlings are weak and get sick.
  • Sowing too deep, so small seeds never come up.
  • Forgetting the label.

lessons.title: Watering and caring for the germinating seed
lessons.html:
Watering sown seed

Seed needs water to start growing. But too much water rots the seed and washes it away.

How to water

  • Use a watering can with a fine rose or a mist nozzle so the drops are soft.
  • Start pouring to the side of the tray, then move over the tray, then move off again. This stops a big splash in one spot.
  • Water until the mix is evenly damp, but not standing in water.
  • For very fine seed, some nurseries water from below: stand the tray in a shallow tray of water for a short time, then lift it out.

Where to put the trays

Put trays where your supervisor shows you: a germination room, a tunnel, a mist bed or a shaded bench. Most seed likes warmth. Some seed needs light to come up, and some needs darkness. The seed packet tells you.

Keeping the right conditions

  • Moisture: check the trays every morning and afternoon. Push a finger gently into the corner. If the top is dry, water lightly.
  • Temperature: read the thermometer and tell your supervisor if it is very hot or cold. On hot Highveld or Lowveld days a tunnel can get too hot.
  • Light and shade: keep shade cloth in place if needed. Strong sun dries trays quickly.
  • Cover: if trays are covered with plastic or glass, wipe off drops and lift the cover a bit each day for air.

Watching the seedlings come up

Look at the trays every day. Write on the record sheet the date when the first seedlings appear. When most seeds are up, remove any cover so the seedlings get air.

Report problems to your supervisor at once:

  • Seedlings falling over at the base (damping off)
  • Green slime or mould on the surface
  • Snails, slugs, ants or birds taking seed
  • No seedlings after the time on the packet

Key points

  • Use clean trays and level, firm seedling mix.
  • Label every tray before sowing.
  • Sow evenly and to the depth on the packet.
  • Water gently with a fine rose; keep the mix damp, not wet.
  • Check trays twice a day and report problems quickly.

quiz.question: Why must you wash old seed trays before using them?

options.text: Dirty trays carry fungus that can kill seedlings

quiz.question: How should you sow very fine, dust-like seed such as petunia?

options.text: Mix it with a little dry sand and sprinkle it on top
Drop all the seed in one corner
Soak it in a bucket for a week

quiz.question: What should you write on the tray label?

options.text: Only the colour of the tray
The plant name, the date and your name or team

quiz.question: Which watering tool is best for freshly sown seed?

options.text: A watering can with a fine rose

quiz.question: What should you do when most seeds have come up under a plastic cover?

options.text: Remove the cover so the seedlings get air

quiz.question: Sowing seed very thickly gives strong seedlings that do not get sick.
You should check the moisture of seed trays every morning and afternoon.
Which problems must you report to your supervisor? (select all that apply)

options.text: Seedlings falling over at the base
Seedlings coming up on the day the packet says
Mould growing on the surface of the mix
